newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 2.71 pct in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 2.71 pct in cautious trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted gains on Friday in a mild recovery that followed Thursday's 4.49 percent plunge, but the market remained cautious amid persisting political concerns, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 41 points, or 2.71 percent higher at 1,552. Over the week, it lost 6.2 percent after last week's 10.34 percent surge caused by easing political tension and privatisation expectations.
Trade volume dropped to 21.83 trillion lira ($172 million) from Thursday's 27.51 trillion ($216.9 million).

Political fears mounted earlier this week due to the ruling Islamist Welfare Party's opposition to a plan to raise compulsory education to eight years from five as part of measures put forward at the military-dominated MGK's February 28 meeting to combat rising Islamist activism.
Several brokers expect the index to drift between 1,500 support and 1,600 resistance next week under the shadow of politics. The market focuses primarily on Monday's MGK meeting.
